bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration with no long-term contracts — Top 10 customers contributed 45.32%, 42.02% and 48.72% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; the top five were approximately 30.26% in FY26 and the single largest customer, Tompkins Industries Inc, 9.34%. The Company does not enter into long-term arrangements with customers, so volumes are re-won order by order.
- Export dependence concentrated on the USA, with unhedged currency exposure — Exports were 29.37%, 28.30% and 33.14% of total revenues in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, of which the USA alone contributed 21.42%, 22.85% and 24.56%. Receivables are largely USD and EUR denominated and the Company does not actively hedge or offset with imports; it separately flags exposure to uncertain tariff structures in North America and Europe.
- Supplier concentration and raw-material price pass-through — Top 10 suppliers accounted for 65.61%, 54.78% and 65.49% of total purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Black/mild steel is the dominant input; price variation clauses exist but negotiation lags and limited pass-through, particularly in export agreements, compress gross margins.
- Execution risk on the Net Proceeds-funded expansion, with machinery orders not yet placed — ₹299.66 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for capacity expansion at Kavathe, Shirwal and Pithampur Unit-I, but the Company confirms it has not placed orders for the machinery; delay in ordering or vendor delivery may cause time and cost overruns, and the deployment has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
- Capacity under-utilisation risk, amplified by the proposed expansion — Blended capacity utilisation (excluding Nashik) was 70.55% in FY26, 66.86% in FY25 and 73.42% in FY24 - it fell in FY25 before recovering. Kavathe already ran at only 60.42% in FY26 and is nonetheless to be expanded by 41.25%, so incremental capacity must find demand to avoid under-absorption of fixed overheads.
- Single-point backward-integration dependency on the Nashik Unit, alongside geographic concentration in Maharashtra — The Nashik Unit is the sole internal source of forgings, a raw material for all five hydraulic-fittings units; the RHP states the fittings units are dependent on its supply, so a shutdown there propagates across the network. Separately, four of six facilities sit in Maharashtra and generated 77.64%, 77.27% and 77.43% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
- Related-party and conflict-of-interest exposure through Promoter Group entities — Promoter Group member Hy-Tech USA Inc. is engaged in a similar line of business (distribution of hydraulic fittings), is the exclusive North America/Canada/Brazil distributor, and accounted for 3.54% of FY26 revenue from operations while sourcing customers contributing a further ₹338.71 million. The Company also extends credit to related party Hy-Tech Fluid Power Private Limited, creating receivables-recovery risk.
- Working capital and receivables intensity — Trade receivables turnover was only 3.96x in FY26 (3.91x FY25, 3.47x FY24) and inventory turnover 2.44x, against an outstanding aggregate borrowing of ₹407.76 million as on June 30, 2026; net capital turnover fell from 4.87x in FY24 to 2.92x in FY26, indicating a lengthening working capital cycle relative to sales.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company intends to expand existing hydraulic-fittings capacity at three of its five fittings units - Shirwal Unit and Kavathe Unit (Satara, Maharashtra) and Pithampur Unit-I (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) - which it says offer the physical space and operational relevance for scaling output. The expansion is machinery-led rather than greenfield: new CNC turning centres, thread rolling machines and CNC vertical machining centres are to be installed to raise throughput, shorten production cycles, improve precision and increase capacity to introduce new SKUs. Against installed capacity as on March 31, 2026 of 144.00 lakh pieces p.a. at Shirwal (utilisation 70.83%), 192.00 lakh pieces p.a. at Kavathe (utilisation 60.42%) and 52.00 lakh pieces p.a. at Pithampur Unit-I (utilisation 84.62%), the proposed additional capacity is 64.80, 79.20 and 43.20 lakh pieces p.a. respectively, taking enhanced capacity to 208.80, 271.20 and 95.20 lakh pieces p.a. - increases of 45.00%, 41.25% and 83.08%, subject to timely commissioning and as certified by an Independent Chartered Engineer on August 5, 2026. The stated rationale is rising demand for hydraulic fittings across sectors and geographies, the need to support entry into defence and railways, and the ability to serve expanded distribution reach. ₹299.66 million of the Net Proceeds (inclusive of GST) is earmarked for this capital expenditure, to be deployed ₹50.00 million in Fiscal 2027 and ₹249.66 million in Fiscal 2028; over the past three Fiscals the Company invested an average of ₹262.42 million per annum in plant and machinery. The Company flags that it has not yet placed orders for the machinery (Risk Factor 11) and that the expansion may not materialise as expected (Risk Factor 17). Backward integration continues to sit at the Nashik Unit (3,120 MT p.a. of forgings, largely captive), which supplies all fittings units - no expansion is proposed there.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Revenue mix across geographies and channels - exports were 29.37% and domestic 70.63% of FY26 revenue; direct/OEM sales 88.42% with the balance from distributors. Export contracts may carry higher margins but bring currency risk and stricter delivery and quality compliance; domestic sales offer lower logistics cost and faster turnaround. Shifts in this mix move realisations, the working capital cycle and the margin profile.
- Sectoral demand cycles - performance is tied to investment and replacement cycles and infrastructure outlays in construction equipment, earthmoving, agricultural machinery and industrial hydraulics; a capex slowdown would hit order volumes, plant utilisation and revenue visibility.
- Customer concentration - approximately 30.26% of FY26 revenues came from the top five customers; loss of any due to insourcing, cost rationalisation or design change would materially affect revenue and profitability. Expanding the customer base and end-user industries is stated as a key strategic priority.
- Input cost volatility - black steel and mild steel are the dominant input cost. Price variation clauses exist in customer contracts but negotiation lags and limited pass-through, particularly in export agreements, can compress gross margins and raise working capital requirements.
- Unhedged foreign currency exposure - export receivables are denominated primarily in USD and EUR; the Company does not engage in active hedging or offsetting imports, leaving margins exposed to exchange-rate volatility.
- Operational efficiency and capacity utilisation - operating leverage depends on utilisation across the Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh facilities; sub-optimal utilisation causes under-absorption of fixed overheads and hits EBITDA margins. Lean manufacturing, line balancing and preventive maintenance are the stated levers.
- Execution of capital expenditure plans - timely commissioning of automation, machining capacity and testing infrastructure is critical to avoid cost overruns, bottlenecks and delayed customer qualification, and drives future revenue scalability, working capital deployment and asset turnover.
- Regulatory and customer-audit compliance - environmental, labour, industrial safety and EXIM requirements plus customer quality certifications (ISO/TS standards) and traceability norms; delays in approvals such as CTO/CTE can raise compliance cost or disrupt operations.
- Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty in North America and Europe - new or higher import duties, withdrawal of preferential access or non-tariff barriers could hurt export price competitiveness, customer ordering patterns and margins.
- Single operating segment - the Company operates in one segment (hydraulic fittings), so no separate segment reporting is made under Ind AS 108; business is stated to be neither seasonal nor cyclical in nature.
- Supplier concentration - top 10 suppliers accounted for 65.61%, 54.78% and 65.49% of total purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration into forging at the Nashik Unit, which manufactures forged components used as raw material by all the other manufacturing units. "We operate with backward integration at our Nashik Unit which is equipped to manufacture forged components which are in turn used at our other facilities to manufacture hydraulic fittings. As of March 31, 2026, we have a total installed capacity of forging capacity of 3,120.00 MT per annum at our Nashik Unit and a manufacturing capacity of 483.00 lakhs pieces per annum of hydraulic fittings across all our other facilities. This backward integration reduces reliance on external suppliers and supports cost efficiency, lead time reduction, and quality control." The Thane, Shirwal, Kavathe and Pithampur units each operate as independent, non-inter-dependent manufacturing units, but all depend on the Nashik Unit for supply of forged components. Manufacturing operations encompass die-designing, forging, heat treatment, machining, plating and inspection and testing, primarily conducted in-house, together with in-house design capability; production infrastructure includes CNC machines, multi-spindle machines, transfer machines, vertical machining centers, thread rolling and centerless grinding machines. A decentralized cell-based manufacturing model is followed, with operations organized into smaller self-contained cells with dedicated oversight for production, quality and design support, plant heads responsible for operational performance and central teams for procurement and strategic planning. On the inbound side, the primary raw material is steel (carbon steel, alloy steel and stainless steel in bars and forgings), majorly sourced from Indian suppliers - imported materials were Rs 3.05 million, Rs 5.68 million and Rs 1.03 million (0.45%, 0.92% and 0.22% of total cost of materials purchased) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Raw materials are procured on purchase orders with no purchase agreements or firm commitments; multiple sources are generally maintained for each major raw material. On the outbound side, a dual-channel model combines direct sales to OEMs and industrial customers with a distributor network, including Promoter Group entity Hy-Tech USA Inc. as exclusive distributor for North America, Canada and Brazil providing local fulfilment and technical support. Quality control comprises a dedicated team of 22 professionals as on March 31, 2026.

Under Regulation 17, the entire pre-Offer equity share capital (other than the Promoters' Contribution) is locked in for six months from the date of Allotment, with the Regulation 17(c) carve-out for VCF/AIF Category I or II/FVCI shares (which must instead be locked in at least six months from date of purchase); no such holders are disclosed here. Anchor Investor lock-in: 50% of Equity Shares Allotted to Anchor Investors locked in for 90 days from the date of Allotment and the remaining 50% for 30 days from the date of Allotment. The Company confirms Promoters' Contribution excludes shares acquired in the three immediately preceding years for consideration other than cash / revaluation of assets / capitalisation of intangible assets, or from bonus issue out of revaluation reserves or unrealised profits or against otherwise ineligible shares; excludes shares acquired in the immediately preceding year below the Offer Price; the Company was not formed by conversion of a partnership/LLP; the Promoters' Contribution shares are not pledged with any creditor; and all Promoter shares are in dematerialised form. Regulation 21 permits pledge of locked-in shares as collateral with a scheduled commercial bank / public financial institution / systemically important NBFC / deposit-accepting HFC subject to conditions (for the 3-year Promoters' Contribution tranche the loan must finance objects of the Offer, which the Company states is not applicable in this Offer). Regulation 22 permits transfer of Regulation 16 locked-in shares to a Promoter Group member or new promoter subject to continuation of lock-in; six-month locked-in shares held by non-Promoters may be transferred to another holder of locked-in shares subject to continuation of lock-in and the Takeover Regulations. overview.business_model: Business-to-business (B2B) manufacture and sale of hydraulic fittings. As of March 31, 2026 the portfolio consists of more than 11,000 stock keeping units (SKUs) of standard fittings (DIN-metric, JIC flared and flareless, O-Ring Face Seal (ORFS) and conversion fittings) plus fittings customised to customer specifications, serving construction machinery, automotive, farming machinery, injection moulding machines and hydraulic systems, with certifications enabling supply to railways and defence. Revenue is earned through two channels: direct engagement with OEMs and other industrial customers (170 direct customers in Fiscal 2026), and a network of authorized distributors and distribution partners (7 in Fiscal 2026) who hold inventory in their territories, promote the products and provide after-sales support; a non-exclusive distribution partner in Europe provides post-sale services, local coordination and logistics support. The Company's own capex spend collapsed while it asks for expansion money: gross additions fell from Rs 359.95 mn (26.13% of revenue, FY24) to Rs 301.77 mn (18.70%, FY25) to Rs 125.54 mn (6.63%, FY26), and capital commitments net of advances at March 31, 2026 were only Rs 27.63 mn.

Working capital absorbs the business: cycle of 194 days (FY26) against 189 in FY24, with inventory at 152 days and trade payable days compressed from 75 to 53 to 49 while receivable days only fell 104 to 91 - net working capital of Rs 625.27 mn sits against net worth of Rs 1,220.17 mn.

The senior layer is almost entirely new while the top is not being renewed: the CFO (Sunil Satwani) and COO (Sandeep Rane) have held their roles only since December 28, 2024 and the Company Secretary since February 05, 2025; KMP attrition was 50.00% in FY24 and 20.00% in FY25 with Senior Management at 45.45% in FY25; the Chairman and Managing Director is 78 on a five-year term from April 01, 2026 and one Whole-time Director is also 78.

Single-point manufacturing dependency: all five hydraulic-fittings units draw forged components from the one 800.00 sq. mtr. leased Nashik Unit, and four of six facilities plus the registered office are leasehold, with balance lease terms of 12 to 56 years.

Input side is more concentrated than the customer side and unprotected by contract: top 10 suppliers were 65.61% of FY26 purchases (top 1 alone 21.62%, up from 13.39%) with no long-term supply agreements, while cost of materials is 41.33% of total expenses.

One third of revenue is unattributed to an end market: 'Others - unidentified sectors sold through distributors' was 34.37% of FY26 revenue from operations, and the issuer states its business 'is not seasonal or cyclical in nature' while 54.82% of revenue comes from construction machinery, farming and automotive, which Risk Factor 8 itself ties to industrial capex cycles and agriculture output.

FY26 growth decelerated sharply and prior-year comparatives carry one-offs: PAT change was minus 35.59% (FY24), plus 69.19% (FY25) and plus 15.16% (FY26); other income fell 24.30% in FY26 on non-recurrence of the Rs 24.00 mn Dindori land gain booked inside FY25 other income.

verdict.our_read: Thane hydraulic-fittings maker, incorporated 1978, six plants (FY26 revenue Rs 1,894.04 mn, EBITDA margin 22.01%, RoCE 24.40%, blended utilisation 70.55%) whose thesis rides on converting Rs 299.66 mn of wholly un-ordered expansion capex into demand it has no order book for.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue from operations Rs 1,377.08 to 1,613.82 to 1,894.04 mn; EBITDA margin 16.38% to 22.18% to 22.01%; PAT Rs 115.96 to 196.19 to 225.92 mn; EPS Rs 1.39 / 2.35 / 2.70. Marked down for the minus 35.59% PAT year in FY24, deceleration to plus 15.16% in FY26, and the Rs 24.00 mn FY25 land gain sitting inside other income.

FY26 CFO Rs 3,032.5 lakhs against PAT Rs 2,259.2 lakhs; total debt Rs 4,083.8 to 4,352.5 to 2,976.3 lakhs; net worth Rs 12,201.7 lakhs; nil contingent liabilities and no covenant breach reported. Held back by a 194-day working-capital cycle, payable days compressed 75 to 49, and cash and cash equivalents of only Rs 263.7 lakhs.

No order book, order in hand or unexecuted value is disclosed anywhere in 416 pages, and all sales are purchase-order based with no fixed-volume commitment; contract liabilities Rs 0.57 mn. Visibility rests solely on 114 repeat customers at 95.10% of FY26 revenue, against blended utilisation that fell to 66.86% in FY25 before recovering to 70.55%.

Rs 299.66 mn of capex is 100% un-ordered per the Chartered Engineer certificate dated August 5, 2026, on 90-day quotations dated July 01-17, 2026 that lapse before the Rs 249.66 mn Fiscal 2028 tranche; contingency only 5% (Rs 14.27 mn); no bank or FI appraisal; no Monitoring Agency since the Rs 600.00 mn Fresh Issue is under the Rs 1,000.00 mn threshold; the general corporate purposes amount and the Total of the utilisation table both print a placeholder.

parameter_scores.basis: Capacity increases of 45.00% (Shirwal), 41.25% (Kavathe) and 83.08% (Pithampur Unit-I) are proposed into units running at 70.83%, 60.42% and 84.62% as on March 31, 2026, with Kavathe already having gone 56.00 to 192.00 lakh pieces p.a. since FY24 at falling utilisation; Consent to Operate for the expanded Shirwal and Pithampur Unit-I is 'Yet to apply'; own capex fell from 26.13% to 6.63% of revenue.

Untraceable Forms 2/18/32 and annual returns to 2002 including the CMD's own 1979 Form 32 and the Promoters' shareholding build-up; both GNL-2 intimations cancelled and re-filed August 6, 2026; MGT-14 adjudication held non-maintainable; DIR-12 date discrepancy for Sunil Prabhakar Sathe (stated by the RHP to be inadvertent and already intimated to the RoC); Rule 11(g) audit-trail modification in all three auditor reports; 18/11/18 statutory-dues delays. Credit for four Independent Directors of eight, five constituted committees, nil pledge and nil KMP attrition in FY26.

Hy-Tech USA Inc. is simultaneously a Promoter Group entity, a declared Common Pursuit in the same line of business, the exclusive North America/Canada/Brazil distributor since April 1, 2022, the fifth largest FY26 customer at 3.54%, the source of a further Rs 338.71 mn (17.88%) of revenue, the recipient of Rs 18.57 mn commission, and a Rs 239.9 lakhs receivable plus Rs 90.0 lakhs payable at March 31, 2026 - with its own financials excluded from the RHP and conflict mechanisms only intended.

Promoters hold 97.99% pre-Offer with nil pledge and have given personal guarantees on the borrowings, and there has been no change of control in five years. Against that: only 13 shareholders in total; the Offer for Sale of up to 14,289,450 shares is entirely by the two Promoter Selling Shareholders at certified average costs of Rs 0.22 and Rs 0.12 per share; the post-Offer promoter percentage and the whole lock-in table are placeholders 'to be updated at the Prospectus stage'.

The RHP states no market share for the Company and cites the CARE Report that more than 90% of the Indian hydraulic fittings industry is unorganised, competitive intensity is high, switching cost for the end user is low and 'the manufacturers may not have significant pricing power'. Offsetting: 11,000+ SKUs, IATF 16949 at three units, IRIS and DRDO approvals, and revenue of Rs 1,894.04 mn against named peers at Rs 4,419.35 mn to Rs 16,213.40 mn.

Top 10 customers 45.32% of FY26 revenue (up from 42.02%) with no long-term arrangements; top 10 suppliers 65.61% of purchases with top 1 at 21.62%; Maharashtra facilities generate 77.64% of revenue and the domestic west and central zones 52.28% and 19.75%; USA alone is 21.42% of revenue; construction machinery, farming and automotive together 54.82%.

Against the Company: 2 indirect-tax proceedings aggregating Rs 12.72 mn, the material one being the Rs 12.69 mn GST show-cause notice of May 14, 2026, above the Rs 8.97 mn materiality threshold, with nil contingent liability recognised. Against Promoters: two pending labour-law complaints (Minimum Wages Act, March 02, 2026 and Payment of Wages Act, April 09, 2026) against Hemant Tukaram Mondkar and Fasto Engineering Private Limited, amount not quantified. A post-DRHP claim of Rs 4.72 mn by Fedex Securities is disputed in its entirety on the ground the engagement terminated in 2022. The single criminal matter names Whole-time Director Sunil Prabhakar Sathe in his then capacity as Chief General Manager of TJSB Sahakari Bank Ltd, unconnected to the Company, as one of 17 accused; that complaint was dismissed by order dated January 30, 2018 and only the complainant's revision application of March 13, 2018 remains pending. Nil against KMPs and SMPs.

CFO and COO in role since December 28, 2024 and Company Secretary since February 05, 2025; KMP attrition 50.00% (FY24) and 20.00% (FY25), Senior Management 45.45% (FY25), both nil in FY26; an Additional Executive Director appointed February 04, 2026 resigned July 01, 2026; the Chairman and Managing Director and one Whole-time Director are both 78, on five-year terms from April 01, 2026; only one of eight Directors has prior listed-company board experience.

red_flags: The entire Rs 299.66 mn capex object is uncommitted, unappraised and unmonitored. Per the Independent Chartered Engineer certificate dated August 5, 2026, orders worth Rs 285.39 mn constituting 100% of the machinery cost 'are yet to be placed'; all 22 line items rest on vendor quotations dated July 01-17, 2026 each stamped 'Validity: 90 days', which lapse around September 29 to October 15, 2026 - while the deployment schedule puts only Rs 50.00 mn in Fiscal 2027 and Rs 249.66 mn in Fiscal 2028, after every quotation has expired, against a 5% (Rs 14.27 mn) contingency. No bank or financial institution has appraised the objects, and no Monitoring Agency will be appointed because the Fresh Issue of Rs 600.00 mn does not exceed the Rs 1,000.00 mn Regulation 41 threshold.

Roughly a fifth of revenue is intermediated by a Promoter Group entity that competes in the same line of business and whose own accounts are excluded from the document. USA revenue was Rs 405.79 mn, 21.42% of FY26 revenue from operations, of which Rs 67.08 mn (3.54%) was sold directly to Hy-Tech USA Inc. and customers sourced by it contributed Rs 338.71 mn (17.88%). Hy-Tech USA Inc. is a Promoter Group member, exclusive distributor for North America, Canada and Brazil under an agreement dated April 1, 2022, the fifth largest customer, took Rs 18.57 mn of commission in FY26, and carried Rs 239.9 lakhs receivable plus Rs 90.0 lakhs commission payable at March 31, 2026. The RHP states it 'is engaged in distribution of hydraulic fittings ... which is similar to the business of the Company' under Common Pursuits, its financials are hosted on the Company website and 'expressly do not form part of' the RHP, and conflict-management mechanisms are described as intended rather than in place - all against a proposed 18% US reciprocal tariff with the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement not concluded.

A dense cluster of self-disclosed compliance defects, several unresolved days before the RHP date. The complete set of corporate resolutions and filings for changes in issued and paid-up capital is untraceable, as are Forms 2, 18 and 32 and annual returns until 2002, share transfer forms dated June 27, 1996 and April 07, 2004, and records for the build-up of the Promoters' own shareholding - including the Form 32 for the Chairman and Managing Director's own appointment as director on January 15, 1979, which is 'not traceable in the records of our Company, nor ... available with the RoC'. An independent practising company secretary (Elias L. Rodrigues & Co., September 3, 2025) confirmed the filings are untraceable at the RoC; both GNL-2 intimations (SRN AB6493032 and AB6494712) were cancelled and had to be re-filed by e-mail and letter dated August 6, 2026, eleven days before this RHP; an adjudication application for the delayed Form MGT-14 was returned non-maintainable.

A Rule 11(g) audit-trail modification recurs in all three years' auditor reports and is still not fully cured. The audit trail was not maintained or preserved for the Nashik Division accounting software until June 24, 2024, and the audit-trail log at the database layer has never been enabled because of the ERP's present design - reported as a modified comment under Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements for FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 and disclosed in Part B(b) of Annexure VII. Offsetting context printed by the issuer: the examination report states the restated information needs no corrective adjustment, the auditors 'did not notice any instance of the audit trail feature being tampered with', and MD&A records no material frauds since incorporation.

The register is three people and the exit is priced off a bonus issue that fell nine days outside the disclosure window. Three Promoters held 81,851,840 shares, 97.99% of pre-Offer capital, and the Company has only 13 shareholders in total. The bonus issue of 82,786,020 shares on February 08, 2025 against a pre-bonus base of 745,820 created effectively the whole present count of 83,531,840, and is the arithmetic reason the auditor-certified average cost of acquisition of the two Promoter Selling Shareholders is Rs 0.22 and Rs 0.12 per share (Ashwin Hemant Mondkar Rs 9.43), against a weighted average cost of Rs 15.12 for shares acquired or sold by way of secondary transactions. The Offer for Sale of up to 14,289,450 shares is entirely theirs and the Company receives none of those proceeds. No bonus ratio is printed for either bonus issue.

A GST demand above the RHP's own materiality threshold sits against a nil contingent liability. A Section 74 CGST show-cause-cum-demand notice dated May 14, 2026 involves Rs 12.69 mn (short payment Rs 11.97 mn on an alleged GSTR-1/IFF versus GSTR-3B mismatch, excess ITC Rs 0.68 mn, ineligible ITC Rs 0.04 mn), refuted by the Company on May 26, 2026 and pending; the RHP's Materiality Threshold is Rs 8.97 mn. Contingent liabilities under Ind AS 37 are stated nil at March 31, 2026, and the RHP warns its litigation amounts exclude interest and penalties 'as not being ascertainable'.

The Nashik Unit operated without a valid Consent to Operate from May 01, 2023 to October 11, 2023, which the RHP itself describes as contravention of the Air Act, the Water Act and the Hazardous Waste Management Rules. No action has been taken to date, and the Government Approvals chapter separately certifies 'Nil' against approvals applied-for-but-not-received, required-but-not-obtained, and expired - a clean present-tense position that does not describe the history. Separately, the Chartered Engineer certificate records Consent to Operate for the expanded Shirwal Unit and Pithampur Unit-I as 'Yet to apply'.

Roughly 29% of revenue is exported with no hedging at all, and the FX line is a material earnings contributor. Exports were 29.37%, 28.30% and 33.14% of revenue in FY26, FY25 and FY24; the Company states it has 'no hedging contracts or policies', does not hedge assets or liabilities, and has never used its sanctioned forward-contract limit (outstanding nil at June 30, 2026 against a Rs 1,000.0 lakhs sanction). Net FX gains were Rs 27.21 mn (1.41% of total income) in FY26 against Rs 9.92 mn and Rs 6.10 mn - an unhedged directional exposure that has so far run favourably.

Statutory-dues discipline has been intermittent across all three years: 18, 11 and 18 instances of delay in FY26, FY25 and FY24 (aggregate amounts delayed Rs 0.17 mn, Rs 0.12 mn and Rs 0.14 mn) across provident fund, ESI, professional tax and TDS/TCS - small in money but persistent in frequency, with TDS-other-than-salary instances rising from 4 to 11 in the latest year.

Board depth for a listed environment is thin: apart from Independent Director Satish Prabhakar Kulkarni (Shree Digvijay Cement Company Limited), no Director has previously served on the board of a listed company, and one Additional Executive Director, Balasubramanian Vishwanathan, was appointed on February 04, 2026 and resigned on July 01, 2026 - under five months, and after the Fiscal in which he was paid Rs 6.0 lakhs of managerial remuneration.
strengths_observed: Profitability step-up held for two years: EBITDA margin 16.38% (FY24) to 22.18% (FY25) to 22.01% (FY26) and PAT Rs 115.96 mn to Rs 196.19 mn to Rs 225.92 mn, on revenue from operations of Rs 1,377.08 mn to Rs 1,613.82 mn to Rs 1,894.04 mn; RoCE 15.24% to 20.46% to 24.40%.

FY26 was self-funding and de-levering: CFO Rs 3,032.5 lakhs against PAT Rs 2,259.2 lakhs (1.34x), total debt down from Rs 4,352.5 lakhs to Rs 2,976.3 lakhs, net worth up from Rs 10,125.1 lakhs to Rs 12,201.7 lakhs, and CFF of minus Rs 2,126.2 lakhs including Rs 743.1 lakhs of long-term repayment.

RoNW of 20.24% (FY26) against the three listed peers the RHP itself names in the same table - Aeroflex Industries 14.06%, Dynamatic Technologies 7.89%, Yuken India 4.27% - on a revenue base of Rs 1,894.04 mn versus Rs 4,419.35 mn, Rs 16,213.40 mn and Rs 4,621.73 mn respectively.

Backward integration insulates the input side from import policy: the Nashik Unit forges 3,120 MTPA (utilisation 49.85% to 59.62% to 67.53%) and supplies all five fittings units, and 99.54% of FY26 raw material (Rs 673.33 mn of Rs 676.44 mn) is sourced within India, with imports of only Rs 3.11 mn.

Revenue is repeat rather than contracted: 114 repeat customers generated Rs 1,800.80 mn, 95.10% of FY26 revenue from operations (FY25 128 customers / 95.20%; FY24 102 / 91.20%), while direct customers grew 144 to 152 to 170 and distributors 5 to 6 to 7.

Receivables quality is clean at the tail: trade receivables beyond one year were Rs 86.8 lakhs at March 31, 2026, equal to 0.71% of net worth, alongside nil contingent liabilities under Ind AS 37 at that date and zero Promoter or Promoter Group shares pledged or otherwise encumbered.

Product-quality cost is low and falling on the volume base: products returned were 0.95% of revenue from operations in FY26 against 1.88% in FY24, with IRIS certification (ISO/TS 22163:2017, awarded Fiscal 2023) and DRDO approval opening railways and defence, though IPE and Railways is still only 1.45% of revenue.

Portfolio breadth is real: more than 11,000 SKUs as of March 31, 2026, with 880 new SKUs added in FY26, 1,676 in FY25 and 2,206 in FY24, across DIN-metric, JIC flared and flareless, ORFS and conversion fittings.
